archetypes.name: Monitor/wall lizard
mustPaint: legs splayed sideways with elbows out; belly near the ground
wedge-shaped scaly head
tail about 1.5x the body (the tail morph then covers skinks through whiptails)
fine scale texture on a plain unmarked mid-tone base (luminance is kept, so any painted mark shows on every species this stands in for)
masks: striped = whiptail/skink stripes, banded = tegu/gila bands, spotted, mottled
archetypes.why: 17 misleading. A scaly sprawling reptile replaces a furry mammal. The heavy lizards (Monitor, Komodo, Tegu, Gila) and the crested iguanas stay caveat. A second, heavy Monitor Lizard painting would lift them later.

archetypes.name: Cat (felid)
mustPaint: round short-muzzled cat head with upright triangular ears (the Civet's long masked snout is what misleads now)
long heavy tail at mid length, so tail 0.7 reads as a bobcat or lynx stub and 1.35 as a snow leopard's rope
deep-chested muscular body on medium legs, stalking pose, big soft paws
plain unmarked tawny coat: no painted spots, rings or face marks

full six-mask set: striped = tiger/tabby stripes, spotted = cheetah/serval solid spots, eye-spotted = open rosettes (leopard, jaguar, snow leopard, ocelot), marbled = clouded-leopard blotches, banded = tail rings, mottled = broken patches
archetypes.why: 10 misleading and 7 caveat cats. Big cats are read by their coat pattern, and only masks on a PLAIN cat can carry it. The Civet's own spots and tail rings show through every tint, so no Civet mask can fix this.

archetypes.name: Antelope
mustPaint: ringed lyre-shaped horns swept up and back
deep chest on very fine long legs with small hooves
short flicking tail; large upright ears on a narrow head
tan flank over a pale belly as soft shading only, with no stripes or face mask
masks: striped = kudu/bongo white flank stripes, banded = gazelle/springbok flank band
archetypes.why: 14 misleading, the biggest hoofed cluster. The horn shape stays wrong for spiral or straight-horned species (Kudu, Eland, Oryx), and Gerenuk's neck is too short, so those are caveat. Every one moves from a spotted small carnivore to a correct horned antelope.

archetypes.name: Stocky rodent
mustPaint: fat barrel body on very short legs
blunt rounded head with small ears set low in the fur
SHORT furry tail, so tail 0.7 reads as tailless (guinea pig, capybara, hyrax, pika, wombat)
plain unmarked brown agouti coat
archetypes.why: 14 misleading. Includes Pika from the Tree Frog and Wombat. Their shared identity is 'round short-legged body, no real tail', which the Civet's long ringed tail breaks. Gopher (incisors) and Agouti (legs) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Perch-like fish
mustPaint: deep laterally compressed body (aspect about 2.5-2.8; the Salmon is about 3.5)
spiny front dorsal fin joined to a soft rear one
big mouth on a sloping face; squared tail; no adipose fin, no kype jaw
plain olive-silver base with a full six-mask set (striped = perch bars, banded, spotted, mottled, marbled, eye-spotted)
archetypes.why: 7 misleading and 7 caveat. The salmon's trout body and hooked jaw are wrong for every spiny-rayed fish.

archetypes.name: Wild cattle
mustPaint: heavy deep barrel body with a straight back on sturdy legs
broad blunt wet muzzle; sideways-set curved horns
tufted rope tail hanging to the hocks
plain unmarked coat, painted as a wild-type ox (no udder, no patches)
archetypes.why: 12 misleading. Bison, Yak and Musk Ox keep a caveat (hump, curtain of hair), and so do the buffalo horn shapes. All read as bovines instead of a civet.

archetypes.name: Monkey
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: primate template + a tail1-3 chain (the primate rig has no tail joints, so a tail can neither scale nor swing)
mustPaint: walking on all fours like the Chimpanzee's pose, but with a slim long-limbed body
tail about body length in a loose curl (0.7 = macaque, 1.35 = spider monkey or langur)
flat forward-facing face with round eyes; small ears
plain unmarked coat, with the cap kept light rather than a hard mark
masks: banded = Lemur ringed tail
archetypes.why: 12 misleading. A tailless ape is the wrong answer for every monkey. Baboon and Mandrill (muzzle) and Lemur, Tamarin and Marmoset stay caveat. Aye-Aye still needs its own painting.

archetypes.name: Reef disc fish
mustPaint: tall round plate-thin disc body (aspect about 1.4)
small pointed mouth; long low dorsal and anal fins
crescent tail
plain base with a full six-mask set (banded = clownfish and butterflyfish bars, eye-spotted = butterflyfish eyespot)
archetypes.why: 12 misleading. Clownfish (rounded fins) and Piranha/Pacu (jaw) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Wolf (canid)
mustPaint: erect triangular ears; narrow pointed muzzle
long legs under a narrow deep chest
bushy tail carried low (tail 1.35 gives the fox brush, 0.7 the dingo)
plain unmarked grizzled grey-tan coat
masks: mottled = African wild dog patchwork
archetypes.why: 11 misleading and 1 caveat. Foxes and the Maned Wolf stay caveat (lower body or stilt legs). If foxes matter, a Red Fox painting later lifts five of them to good.

archetypes.name: Sea/shore gull
mustPaint: standing, with long narrow pointed wings folded to cross beyond the tail
webbed feet; stout hook-tipped bill
white body with a grey mantle as shading only
tail at mid length so 1.35 approximates tern and tropicbird streamers
archetypes.why: 11 misleading. Seabirds are long-winged web-footed birds, not a hook-billed raptor with talons. Tern, Tropicbird and Frigatebird (forked or streamer tails, pouch) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Otter (mustelid)
mustPaint: long low tubular body on short legs
thick tail tapering to a point
blunt whiskered head with small ears
plain unmarked coat
archetypes.why: 7 misleading and 3 caveat. Weasel, Stoat and Mink stay caveat (slimmer), and so does Sea Otter (floats on its back).

archetypes.name: Brown bear (bear)
mustPaint: muscular shoulder hump; broad dished head with small round ears
flat-footed plantigrade paws with long claws; stub tail (tail 0.7)
plain unmarked coat that reads as a polar bear under a white palette
masks: eye-spotted = eye patches (Panda, Spectacled Bear), banded = chest crescent or shoulder band (Sun Bear, Panda)
archetypes.why: 9 misleading, the whole bear family. Panda and Spectacled/Sun Bear rely on the mask. Check that their pattern genes select those masks.

archetypes.name: Goose (waterfowl)
mustPaint: heavy body on webbed feet set well back
medium-long upright neck, between duck and swan
flat rounded bill
plain grey-brown
archetypes.why: 9 misleading. Swan (longer neck), Loon/Grebe (dagger bill) and Coot/Moorhen (frontal shield) stay caveat. All of them lose the raptor bill and talons.

archetypes.name: Slender colubrid
mustPaint: very slender whip body in a fast S-curve
narrow rounded head with a large round eye
plain smooth glossy scales (no python net)
masks: striped = lengthwise garter stripes, banded = king-snake rings
archetypes.why: 2 misleading and 7 caveat. Replaces the heavy netted python for every slim snake.

archetypes.name: Heron (long-neck wader)
mustPaint: long S-kinked neck; heavy dagger bill
stilt legs with long toes
slim upright wader body, plain grey
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Neck and leg length cannot be morphed, so waders need their own painting. Ibis, Spoonbill and Flamingo (bill shape) and Crane (bustle) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Songbird
mustPaint: small round-headed perching bird on thin legs
stout conical bill; short square tail
plain brown, only lightly streaked, so colour genes read
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Robin and Starling (thin bill) and Cardinal (crest) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Gamebird
mustPaint: plump rounded ground bird on short legs; small head
short rounded bill; short broad tail (fannable)
barred but low-contrast plumage; feathered feet
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Turkey, Chicken (comb, wattle) and Hoatzin (crest) stay caveat. The long-tailed gamebirds go to the Pheasant painting.

archetypes.name: Shorebird
mustPaint: horizontal crouched body on long thin legs
straight probing bill about head length
plain brown-grey upperparts
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Curlew and Avocet (curved bills) and Rail (narrow body, long toes) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Bovid goat
mustPaint: backward-arcing ridged horns
chin beard; short upright tail
stocky muscular body on sturdy legs
plain unmarked coat
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Sheep (fleece), Wild Sheep (curled horns) and Mountain Goat (shaggy white) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Shark
mustPaint: tall triangular first dorsal; asymmetric tail with a long upper lobe
row of gill slits; crescent mouth under a conical snout
grey back over a white belly as shading
masks: striped = tiger-shark bars, spotted = whale-shark checkerboard
archetypes.why: 8 misleading. Whale and Basking Shark (giant mouths) stay caveat. Hammerhead needs its own head.

archetypes.name: Pike
mustPaint: elongate torpedo body (aspect about 5)
long flattened toothy snout; dorsal fin set far back near the tail
plain mottled green, with no painted bean spots
archetypes.why: 3 misleading and 5 caveat. Gar (beak) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Closed-shell beetle
archetypes.bodyPlan: insect (wing cases closed, flight wings hidden)
mustPaint: smooth closed domed oval wing cases; head tucked under the pronotum
walking pose
masks: spotted = ladybug spots, mottled = carrion beetle blotches, banded = diving beetle rim
archetypes.why: Caveat only (8). The Beetle painting holds its wing cases raised in flight. Second tier.

archetypes.name: Herring
mustPaint: slim mirror-silver body; a single mid-back dorsal
deeply forked tail; large eye
no spots (unlike the Salmon)

archetypes.name: Equid
mustPaint: stiff upright brush mane; single hooves on slim legs
tufted tail; large head on an arched neck
plain unmarked dun coat
masks: striped = zebra stripes including the legs (the closest this can get to Okapi's leg stripes)
archetypes.why: 7 misleading. Zebra relies on the striped mask. Donkey and Wild Ass (long ears) and Okapi stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Salamander
mustPaint: moist smooth scaleless skin (which is why a lizard painting will not do)
blunt rounded head; four short splayed limbs of equal size
long rounded tail about body length
plain dark base; masks: spotted = fire-salamander spots
archetypes.why: 7 misleading. Axolotl, Olm and Blind Salamander stay caveat because nobody painted external gills.

archetypes.name: Eel
archetypes.bodyPlan: serpent (the eel profile already lists it; the undulation needs the segment chain)
mustPaint: snake-like body with a continuous fin fringe along back, tail and belly
blunt-jawed head; no pelvic fins
plain olive-brown
archetypes.why: 7 misleading. Lamprey (sucker mouth), Moray (gape) and Oarfish (red crest) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Bee
mustPaint: furry thorax; banded abdomen (shading only; the bands come from the banded mask)
two pairs of clear wings
pinched waist
archetypes.why: 7 misleading. Bumblebee, Wasp, Fly and Black Fly stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Rat
mustPaint: long naked scaly tail about body length
pointed whiskered snout; rounded thin ears
hunched arched back on short legs
plain unmarked coat
archetypes.why: 6 misleading. Shrew (proboscis snout) and Possum (white face) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Hare
mustPaint: very long upright ears, painted hare-long because they only scale slightly with the head
long rangy hind legs and big hind feet; crouched ready-to-bound pose
powder-puff tail; plain brown coat
archetypes.why: 6 misleading, all currently shown as a leaping tree frog. Rabbit (shorter ears) and Mara stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Pond turtle
mustPaint: domed shell with a scute mosaic over the whole trunk (the shell rides the spine and chest bones)
head extended on a wrinkled neck; stumpy clawed webbed feet
short tail
archetypes.why: 6 misleading. Snapping Turtle (big head, saw tail), Softshell (flat leathery shell) and Tortoise (tall dome) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Dolphin
archetypes.bodyPlan: fish (the fluke rides the caudal joint; the side view hides its horizontal axis)
mustPaint: sickle dorsal fin; short beak with a smiling jawline
smooth grey countershaded skin; paddle flippers; tail flukes
masks: a black-and-white saddle and eye-patch pied mask for Orca, drawn in whichever pattern slot Orca's gene selects
archetypes.why: 6 misleading. River Dolphin (long beak) and Pilot Whale (melon) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Great whale
mustPaint: huge streamlined body; tiny nub dorsal set far back (reads as 'no dorsal' for Right Whale, Gray Whale and Beluga)
broad flat rostrum; throat pleats; long flippers; wide flukes
plain blue-grey
archetypes.why: 6 misleading. Humpback (long white flippers), Right Whale (callosities) and Beluga (melon) stay caveat. Sperm Whale and Narwhal need their own paintings.

archetypes.name: Frog (sitting)
mustPaint: squat sitting crouch with folded hind legs
wide flat head with an eardrum disc and a wide mouth line
smooth plain skin (warts would leak onto dart frogs)
masks: spotted/banded/marbled = dart-frog warning blotches, striped = dorsolateral ridges
archetypes.why: 1 misleading and 5 caveat. The tree frog's leap, red eye and toe pads are wrong for ground frogs.

archetypes.name: Pig
mustPaint: wedge snout ending in a flat disc; small upcurved tusks
high bristly shoulders sloping to a low rump on short legs
thin tail; plain grey-brown
archetypes.why: 5 misleading. Warthog (warts, big tusks) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Deer
mustPaint: branched sweeping antlers (rigid on the head bone)
slender legs, long thin neck, large cupped ears
plain unmarked coat with the pale rump patch as shading only
archetypes.why: 5 misleading. Moose (palmate antlers, dewlap) and Reindeer/Caribou (brow shovel, neck ruff) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Corvid
mustPaint: stout straight pointed bill
square-to-wedge tail
paint it mid-grey rather than jet black, so near-grey tinting can colour Jays and Choughs

archetypes.name: Crocodilian
mustPaint: long flat armoured snout; scute rows along back and tail
low sprawling legs; heavy tail longer than the body

archetypes.name: Elephant
archetypes.bodyPlan: quadruped (trunk and tusks ride the head and jaw; a trunk chain is a later motion upgrade)
mustPaint: trunk reaching the ground; curved tusks
huge fan ears
pillar legs; plain grey wrinkled hide
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Asian Elephant (small ears, domed head) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Parrot
mustPaint: short deeply hooked beak; zygodactyl feet
compact body with a mid-length tail (1.35 approximates a macaw)
plain green base
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Cockatoo (crest) and Kakapo stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Ratite
mustPaint: long bare neck with a small flat head
long powerful bare legs
shaggy plumage, no flight wings shown

archetypes.name: Pheasant
mustPaint: long pointed trailing tail (a painted long tail is the only way a bird gets one)
red bare face wattle; ground-bird body
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Peacock (train, crest) and Quetzal stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Auk
mustPaint: fully upright stance on rear-set feet
small stiff wings held at the sides
black back over a white front
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Puffin (bill) and Penguin (flippers) stay caveat. A Penguin painting is worth doing later because players recognise it instantly.

archetypes.name: Secretary bird
mustPaint: very long bare legs
long tail
crest behind a short hooked head
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Bustard and Roadrunner stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Grasshopper
mustPaint: huge angled jumping hind legs rising above the back
wings folded flat along the back
tall flat-sided head
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. Cave Cricket (hump, whip antennae) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Stonefly
mustPaint: soft elongate body with wings folded flat and overlapping
long antennae; short tail cerci
archetypes.why: 4 misleading. All except Stonefly stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Stingray
archetypes.bodyPlan: fish (the pectoral joints drive the wings; a real wing chain is a later motion upgrade)
mustPaint: flat kite disc of fused pectoral wings
long whip tail
eyes on top

archetypes.name: Viper
mustPaint: broad triangular head on a thin neck
short thick body coiled, neck in an S
zigzag dorsal band
archetypes.why: 3 misleading and 1 caveat. Rattlesnake (rattle) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Cod
mustPaint: three dorsal fins; chin barbel
pale lateral line

archetypes.name: Hedgehog (spiny)
mustPaint: dense cape of spines over a loaf-shaped body; short legs
pointed snout; tiny tail
archetypes.why: 3 misleading. Porcupine (long quills) and Echidna (beak) stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Owl
mustPaint: flat round facial disc with huge forward-facing eyes
upright barrel body, no visible neck; feathered legs

archetypes.name: Pigeon
mustPaint: small round head on a deep chest
short legs; slender bill

archetypes.name: Butterfly
mustPaint: two pairs of broad scaled wings (the accent group, so they take the accent colour)
clubbed antennae
masks: eye-spotted = wing eyespots
archetypes.why: 3 misleading. Moth and Caddisfly stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Dragonfly
mustPaint: two pairs of long net-veined wings held flat
huge globe eyes
long rod abdomen

archetypes.name: Ant
mustPaint: three body lumps pinched at a narrow waist
elbowed antennae
no wings

archetypes.name: Kangaroo
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: macropod = hopper template + a tail chain (the tail is a third leg; the hopper rig has none)
mustPaint: massive hind legs and long feet in an upright stance
thick tapering tail resting on the ground
tiny forearms

archetypes.name: Sea lion
archetypes.bodyPlan: quadruped (flippers on the leg chains; sea lions walk on all four)
mustPaint: fore-flippers propping the chest up
small ear flaps; dog-like whiskered muzzle
smooth wet coat
archetypes.why: 3 misleading. Seal (no ear flaps, trailing hind flippers) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Hyena
mustPaint: back sloping steeply from high shoulders
thick neck, heavy jaws, round ears
plain base; masks: spotted, and striped for Striped Hyena

archetypes.name: Camel
mustPaint: single hump
long curved neck
long knobbly legs

archetypes.name: Gliding mammal
archetypes.bodyPlan: flyer-membrane (forelimbs on the wing chains, hind limbs on the leg chains, the patagium painted between them)
mustPaint: membrane spread from wrist to ankle in a glide
big black eyes
flattened furry tail

archetypes.name: Billfish
mustPaint: long spear bill
sickle dorsal; stiff crescent tail

archetypes.name: Jellyfish
archetypes.bodyPlan: radial (the rig already has a bell joint)
mustPaint: translucent domed bell
long trailing tentacles and frilled oral arms
emissive glow welcome
archetypes.why: 3 misleading. Man-of-War and Comb Jelly stay caveat.

archetypes.name: Coral
mustPaint: branching stony colony
cup polyps at the tips
pale base so white corals read

archetypes.name: Squid
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: decapod cephalopod = cephalopod template + two long tentacle chains + mantle fin joints
mustPaint: torpedo mantle with rear fins
eight arms plus two long clubbed tentacles
large eye

archetypes.name: Squirrel
mustPaint: bushy plumed tail arched over the back
large dark eye; rounded ears
masks: striped = chipmunk stripes

archetypes.name: Badger
mustPaint: broad flattened low body
long digging foreclaws
keep the face stripe faint so Wolverine and Devil are not striped

archetypes.name: Tuna
mustPaint: stiff crescent tail on a keeled stalk
finlets to the tail; fat torpedo body

archetypes.name: Armoured insectivore
mustPaint: overlapping armour scales over body and tail
small conical head, no teeth

archetypes.name: Kingfisher
mustPaint: dagger bill longer than the head
oversized head with no visible neck; stubby body and very short tail

archetypes.name: Toucan
mustPaint: oversized bill nearly as long as the body, left plain so the palette colours it
long broad tail; bare eye skin

archetypes.name: Swallow
mustPaint: long narrow swept-back wings
deeply forked tail; tiny bill with a wide gape
archetypes.why: 2 misleading. Swift (scythe wings, no fork) stays caveat.

archetypes.name: Llama
mustPaint: long upright neck, no hump
long banana ears

archetypes.name: Tapir
mustPaint: short flexible proboscis
rounded high rump

archetypes.name: Fangtooth
mustPaint: huge blunt head with oversized fangs
short dark body; small fins

archetypes.name: Anglerfish
mustPaint: glowing lure on a stalk (emissive)
enormous upturned fanged jaw; globular body

archetypes.name: Dragonfish
mustPaint: slim black body with photophore rows
fangs reaching past the eyes

archetypes.name: Flatfish
mustPaint: flat oval body with a continuous fin skirt
both eyes on the upper side

archetypes.name: Bonytongue
mustPaint: long body with the dorsal and anal fins set far back
red-edged armoured scales; upturned mouth

archetypes.name: Catfish
mustPaint: broad flat scaleless head
long barbel whiskers

archetypes.name: Pufferfish
mustPaint: round body; big eyes; beaked mouth
tiny fins

archetypes.name: Flying fish
mustPaint: huge wing-like pectoral fins spread
long lower tail lobe

archetypes.name: Manatee
mustPaint: barrel body, front flippers, paddle tail
bristly downturned muzzle

archetypes.name: Dumbo octopus
mustPaint: webbed umbrella between the eight arms
ear-like fins on the mantle

archetypes.name: Tick
mustPaint: flat teardrop body
eight short legs bunched at the front

archetypes.name: Harvestman
mustPaint: tiny pea body
eight thread-thin legs many times the body length

archetypes.name: Aphid
mustPaint: soft pear-shaped body
short antennae; tiny legs

archetypes.name: Scorpion
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: arachnid template + a metasoma tail chain (sting) + pedipalp chelae
mustPaint: pincer claws held forward
segmented tail arched over the back, ending in a sting

archetypes.name: Millipede
mustPaint: cylindrical ringed tube body
two short legs per segment in a rippling fringe

archetypes.name: Giraffe
mustPaint: enormously long neck; ossicones; steeply sloping back

archetypes.name: Rhinoceros
mustPaint: nose horn; plated folded hide; stumpy legs

archetypes.name: Hippopotamus
mustPaint: barrel body; huge square muzzle; eyes and ears on top of the head

archetypes.name: Sloth
archetypes.bodyPlan: quadruped (hanging pose; limbs on the leg chains)
mustPaint: long hook claws; round smiling face; shaggy fur

archetypes.name: Giant anteater
mustPaint: long tubular snout; huge flag tail; shoulder wedge

archetypes.name: Aardvark
mustPaint: tubular pig snout; tall rabbit ears; thick tapering tail

archetypes.name: Mole
mustPaint: spade forepaws; pink pointed snout; neckless body

archetypes.name: Beaver
mustPaint: flat scaly paddle tail; orange incisors; humped body

archetypes.name: Koala
mustPaint: huge fluffy ears; spoon nose; no tail

archetypes.name: Platypus
mustPaint: duck bill; flat paddle tail; webbed feet

archetypes.name: Meerkat
mustPaint: standing upright on the hind legs and tail; dark eye rings

archetypes.name: Walrus
mustPaint: long tusks; bristle moustache; blubbery body

archetypes.name: Sea turtle
mustPaint: teardrop shell; long wing-like front flippers

archetypes.name: Horned lizard
mustPaint: crown of horns; flat round pancake body

archetypes.name: Chameleon
mustPaint: turret eyes; coiled tail; casque; leaf-flat body

archetypes.name: Frilled lizard
mustPaint: huge circular neck frill; gaping mouth

archetypes.name: Aye-aye
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: primate + tail chain (as for Monkey)
mustPaint: huge bare ears; wire-thin middle finger; shaggy tail

archetypes.name: Hummingbird
mustPaint: needle bill; blurred narrow wings; iridescent gorget

archetypes.name: Woodpecker
mustPaint: chisel bill; stiff tail braced on the bark

archetypes.name: Cormorant
mustPaint: snaky neck; hooked bill; wings held open

archetypes.name: Pelican
mustPaint: huge bill with a throat pouch; short legs

archetypes.name: Kiwi

archetypes.name: Cobra
mustPaint: flared hood; front third reared vertically

archetypes.name: Mantis
mustPaint: folded raptorial forelegs; triangular head on a neck

archetypes.name: Cicada
mustPaint: tented clear wings; blunt wide head; barrel body

archetypes.name: Stick insect
mustPaint: twig-thin body; legs stretched in line with it

archetypes.name: Water strider
mustPaint: extremely long splayed middle and hind legs

archetypes.name: Giant water bug
mustPaint: flat oval leaf-shaped body; raptorial front legs

archetypes.name: Mosquito
mustPaint: needle proboscis; very long dangling legs

archetypes.name: Pseudoscorpion

archetypes.name: Camel spider

archetypes.name: Hammerhead
mustPaint: T-shaped hammer head with the eyes at the tips

archetypes.name: Sturgeon

mustPaint: long paddle rostrum; gaping mouth

archetypes.name: Pipefish

archetypes.name: Lionfish

archetypes.name: Mudskipper
mustPaint: periscope eyes; propped up on arm-like pectorals

archetypes.name: Sand dollar

archetypes.name: Sea cucumber

archetypes.name: Nautilus
archetypes.bodyPlan: NEW: shelled cephalopod = rigid coiled shell + a fan of short tentacles
mustPaint: striped coiled shell; many short tentacles; hood

masks.why: The cheapest lift in the plan: these three caveat snakes lack only a pattern. Paint striped as lengthwise dorsal stripes (Garter), banded as full rings (King Snake) and mottled as saddle blotches (Boa). About 15% of the python's net still shows through. If the Racer painting lands first, Garter and King Snake move there, but Boa stays on the Python. Today a pattern gene on the Python renders plain, so this set also makes every patterned serpent genome, bred or alien, show its markings.

Carrion Beetle lacks only its black-and-orange blotched wing cases, which the mottled mask restores. Ladybug (spotted) and Diving Beetle (banded rim) gain their pattern but stay caveat, because this painting holds the wing cases raised in flight. Their fix is the Closed-shell beetle painting, which should carry its own copy of this set.

Partial only. Poison Dart Frog gets its warning blotches but keeps the red eye and toe pads, so nothing reaches good. Paint the dart-frog masks on the new sitting Bullfrog painting instead. Do this set only so bred and alien hoppers show their pattern gene.

Partial only. Kestrel (spotted back, banded tail) and Harpy Eagle (banded chest) gain a marking but keep the wrong silhouette (pointed falcon wings, split crest). Low value: give the new bird paintings their own sets instead. No new mask is proposed for the Civet either. Its own painted spots and tail rings show under any mask, so its felid caveats are fixed by the plain Cougar painting instead.

noStandInPlans.plan: Wire the profile first: small-crustacean has candidateTemplates [] even though the template already exists in tools/creature-animation/specialized-templates.mjs. Template: crustacean-small (5 leg pairs, 6 abdomen segments, tail fan). Paint a side-on shrimp with a curved segmented abdomen and a spread tail fan, stalked eyes, a serrated rostrum and very long whip antennae, on a plain translucent base. Cave Shrimp and Vent Shrimp read by palette; Krill, Brine Shrimp, Fairy Shrimp and Amphipod are caveat.

Wire the profile first (annelid-land/annelid-water have candidateTemplates []). Template: annelid (12-segment wave). Paint a ringed smooth tube with a clitellum and no limbs, in plain pink-brown. Ice Worm, Leech and Fly Larvae read by palette; Marine Worm, Polychaete Worm and Scale Worm (bristles, scales) are caveat. Also point Caecilian's profile at annelid: it is misleading on the Python today, and its ringed grooves and eyeless head are closer to the worm.

Wire the profile first (land-gastropod/water-gastropod have candidateTemplates []). Template: gastropod (4-joint foot wave, rigid shell, eye stalks). Paint a coiled spiral shell on a gliding foot with two eye tentacles, and keep the shell plain so marine snails recolour. Conch (flared lip) and Cowrie (egg-shaped shell) are caveat.

Wire the profile first (bivalve has candidateTemplates []). Template: bivalve (hinge, two valves, mantle, optional siphon and foot). Paint two symmetric hinged valves slightly agape, with concentric growth rings and a pale foot showing. Razor Clam, Scallop and Giant Clam are caveat on shape.

Wire the profile first. Template: crustacean-small with the optional tail fan omitted. Paint a teardrop body wide at the front, with long outstretched antennae and a forked tail. Water Flea and Tadpole Shrimp are caveat.

Wire the profile first (Flatworm's profile also needs gastropod added). Template: gastropod with the optional shell absent. Paint a shell-less slug on a gliding foot with two tentacle pairs and a mantle saddle. Nudibranch (gill plume) and Flatworm (ribbon body, no tentacles) are caveat.

Wire the profile first. Template: gastropod with the shell drawn as a low uncoiled cone, clamped flat. Paint a ribbed hat-shaped cone flush on rock. Abalone (ear shape, holes) and Chiton (eight plates) are caveat.

Wire the profiles first (annelid-water and cnidarian). Template: sessile-filter (anchored base, body, crown, aperture). Paint a squat column fixed by a basal disc under a dense crown of soft tentacles. Also move Sea Anemone off the Starfish, where it is misleading today. Tube Worm and Giant Tube Worm (white tube, red plume) are caveat.

Wire the profile first (clawed-crustacean has candidateTemplates []). Template: crustacean-clawed (claws, 4 leg pairs, abdomen with tail fan, antennae). Paint two big forward pincers, a segmented tail ending in a fan, and long whip antennae.
Wire the profile first. Template: crustacean-small. Paint overlapping armour plates like a pill bug, seven similar leg pairs and two tail uropods.
Wire the profile first (sponge/tunicate have candidateTemplates []). Template: sessile-filter. Paint a porous vase or tube with a large osculum and no symmetry. Sea Squirt (two siphons) is caveat.

Wire the profile first. Template: colonial-filter (4-segment drift chain plus an aperture). Paint a translucent hollow tube open at one end, pimpled with zooids, with an emissive blue glow. Salp is caveat.
Wire the profile first. Template: crustacean-clawed, with a borrowed spiral shell painted rigid over the abdomen, one enlarged claw and stalked eyes.

Template: brachyuran, the rig that already carries five painted crabs. Now: move Fiddler Crab's profile from clawed-crustacean to brachyuran, so the painted Crab stands in (caveat: its claws are equal). Later: paint a Fiddler Crab with one oversized claw and tall stalked eyes.
Wire the profile first. Template: barnacle (anchored cone, trapdoor plates, six cirri). Paint a chalky volcano cone with feathery cirri sweeping out.
Wire the profile first. Template: xiphosuran. Paint a smooth domed horseshoe carapace with a long rigid spike tail and the legs hidden.
Wire the profile first. Template: lobopod (4 segments, 4 leg pairs). Paint a plump segmented barrel on eight stubby clawed legs, with a tube mouth.

summary: 454 of 631 Earth species are misleading today because each body plan has only one painting, and the Civet (185), Eagle (92) and Salmon (90) are stretched over whole classes. Breadth beats fidelity: the top 10 new paintings (Wall Lizard, Cougar, Impala, Marmot, Bass, Cattle, Capuchin, Tang, Wolf, Gull) fix 120 misleading species, the top 20 fix 195 and the top 35 fix 267, while the last 53 paintings cover one species each. Paint every new archetype on a PLAIN base coat and put its patterns in its own six-mask set: the morph keeps luminance, so the Civet's spots and ringed tail show on everything it stands in for, and that is why no Civet mask can make a tiger. Cheap wins that need no new painting: a mask set on the Python lifts Garter Snake, King Snake and Boa to good, one on the Beetle lifts Carrion Beetle, and moving Fiddler Crab's profile to brachyuran lets the painted Crab stand in. The 53 species with no stand-in need their profiles pointed at specialized templates that already exist but are unused (crustacean-small, annelid, gastropod, bivalve, sessile-filter and others); after that, four paintings (Shrimp, Earthworm, Snail, Clam) cover 29 of them, plus Caecilian. Five archetypes need a rig change before they are painted: primate + tail (Capuchin, Aye-Aye), hopper + tail (Kangaroo), decapod cephalopod (Squid), arachnid + tail (Scorpion) and shelled cephalopod (Nautilus). A mask shows only when the species' own pattern gene selects it, so check the genes before painting a named species' mask (for example Tiger and Zebra on striped, Panda on eye-spotted, Garter Snake on striped). The caveat-only paintings (Closed-shell beetle, Herring, Cod, Tuna) rank high by count but should come after the misleading fixes.
